c.tagline: Israel's Red Sea playground - year-round sun, coral reefs, and duty-free desert nights.

taxi.fareNote: Metered white taxis are standard - ask the driver to run the meter (moneh). The Gett app is the local ride-hailing option; Uber does not operate in Israel.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

solo.f: Government travel advisory is the main factor (35/100)

avoid.reason: Safe resort; follow local security guidance

hood_desc: Eilat's flagship shore - a palm-lined promenade backed by the biggest five-star resorts (Herods, Dan, Royal Beach), with the main swimming beach, restaurants, and sunset views over the Red Sea. The classic first-timer base.
The inner saltwater lagoon ringed by hotels, the yacht marina, boardwalk bars, and the Ice Mall; buzzy day and night and walkable to just about everything.
A cluster of mid-range hotels, pubs, and nightclubs a short walk from the lagoon; the go-to for budget-conscious travelers who want nightlife on the doorstep.
The workaday downtown around HaTmarim Boulevard and the central bus station - hostels, cheaper hotels, supermarkets, and local eateries, about a 15-minute walk from the beach.
The quieter southern coast 5-7 km toward the Taba border, home to the Coral Beach Nature Reserve, the Underwater Observatory, and Eilat's best shore diving and snorkeling; low-key and reef-focused.

water.note: Desalinated tap water is safe, though many prefer bottled for taste.

transit.hours: Buses run roughly 6:00 AM to around midnight and do not operate on Shabbat (Friday evening to Saturday evening); taxis and the Gett app fill that gap.
transit.note: Eilat has no rail or metro; the city runs on Egged buses (line 15 to Coral Beach, line 30 to Ramon Airport), taxis, and the Gett app, plus easy walking along the beachfront.
transit.pay: Bus fares are paid with a Rav-Kav smartcard or contactless card (around ₪5-6 a ride); taxis run on a meter.

bus: Egged intercity lines 390/394 to Tel Aviv and Jerusalem (~4-5h)
train: No railway serves Eilat; a line has long been proposed but not built

landmarks: Coral Beach Nature Reserve
A protected Red Sea reef right off the shore, where snorkelers drift over technicolor coral gardens teeming with parrotfish, lionfish and sea turtles.
Underwater Observatory Marine Park
Descend below the waves in this iconic white tower to watch sharks, rays and reef fish glide past panoramic windows six meters underwater.
Dolphin Reef
A laid-back beach sanctuary where bottlenose dolphins swim freely, letting visitors observe or snorkel alongside them in the warm Red Sea shallows.
Eilat Promenade (Tayelet)
The buzzing seafront boardwalk linking North Beach's hotels, marinas and cafes, perfect for sunset strolls with Jordan's mountains shimmering across the gulf.
Hai-Bar Yotvata Nature Reserve
A desert wildlife reserve breeding biblical-era animals like oryx, addax and onagers, which roam freely across a savannah-like stretch of the Arava Valley.
Mount Tzfahot
A rewarding desert summit hike above Coral Beach delivering a four-country panorama over Israel, Egypt, Jordan and Saudi Arabia at sunset.
Botanical Garden of Eilat
An improbable man-made rainforest oasis on a desert hillside, with waterfalls, organic orchards and shaded lookout points over the Red Sea.
Ice Mall Eilat
A glacier-themed shopping mall with a full-size ice-skating rink at its heart, a deliciously surreal escape from the year-round desert heat.
Eilat Birdwatching Park (IBRCE)
A free wetland reserve near the Jordanian border where hundreds of millions of migratory birds refuel each year on the only land bridge linking Europe, Asia and Africa.
Eilat Light (Lighthouse Beach)
A lighthouse perched on a bluff above the Gulf of Aqaba near the Egyptian border, with a wild, undeveloped beach below popular for camping and snorkeling.

train.note: No passenger railway reaches Eilat; a line has long been proposed but never built, so travel is by air, bus, or car.

bus.note: Egged runs long-distance coaches (lines 390/394) from Eilat's central bus station to Tel Aviv and Jerusalem in about 4-5 hours; buses do not run on Shabbat (Friday evening to Saturday evening).

ferry.note: Eilat's port on the Gulf of Aqaba handles cargo and a small marina but has no scheduled passenger ferry; the boats leaving the marina are glass-bottom, dive and pleasure craft rather than transport. The nearest sea crossing is from Aqaba in Jordan, about an hour away through the Yitzhak Rabin/Wadi Araba land border, where AB Maritime runs ferries across the gulf to Nuweiba in Egypt. Sailing directly between an Israeli port and a neighbouring one is not possible, so any onward sea journey means crossing a land border first.
